chapter: Looking back: rock, blues, childhood and guitar innovators
title: Tal Farlow, Wes Montgomery, Joe Pass and other guitarists
summary: Collins calls Wes Montgomery the most lyrical guitarist and lists Joe Pass, Pat Martino, Lee Ritenour and Howard Roberts.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: After Charlie I think Tal Farlow came through with bebop. Playing. And I think one of the great innovators of our time, and who was Wes Montgomery. Wes Montgomery in my estimation was one of the most lyrical guitarists I've ever heard. That includes everybody. He came closer to having it all as far as chords, as far as single strings, just -- he was just sheer beauty. Wes Montgomery.

Speaking of being fortunate to be around in this time, I'll have to go along with that, as far as he's concerned also, because he did something. I've heard guys with an awful lot of technique and everything, but the lines that Wes Montgomery played were the most interesting lines. And the -- his chord, just beautiful chords. He came closer to having it all, than anybody I know. And of course Joe Pass, what can I say. Joe Pass is also a great guitarist. He's a stylist. Yeah. But of the young crop I think we're going to have - Pat Martina is a young guitarist we're going to hear a lot about from.

And Lee Ritenour. I look for a lot of great things from Lee Ritenour. He's got youth, he's got -- he's a very intelligent player. You know. And he's a marvelous musician. And I also like Howard Roberts. Howard is a marvelous guitarist, you know. So there are some very good guitarists around, and of course wait a minute.
